Senses.PreferredTarget: a lid fitting the box, heaven and earth
AlternateTargets: box and lid, heaven and earth
lid matching box — heaven and earth
Senses.Explanation: The components mean “box or case” (函), “lid or cover” (蓋), and “heaven and earth,” literally qian and kun, the first two trigrams of the Book of Changes (乾坤): "a lid fitting the box, heaven and earth." The corpus attests (函蓋) as a box and its lid that correspond — the collocation (函蓋相稱) / (函蓋相應) recurs (e.g. B25n0144 著函，函蓋相稱故, "[the lid] on the box, because box and lid correspond"), and (乾坤) is the standard pairing for the whole cosmos. The phrase is the FIRST of the (雲門三句) (Yunmen's three phrases), paired with (截斷眾流) and (隨波逐浪). Its attested history in the corpus: Yunmen (雲門文偃) delivers it in his own (廣錄) as a (示眾) — (函蓋乾坤目機銖兩)。(不涉春緣) (T47n1988; this edition reads 不涉春緣, where other editions read 不涉萬緣); his heir (德山緣密) (德山圓明密) (遂離其語為三句) — "then separated his words into three phrases": (函蓋乾坤句)、(截斷眾流句)、(隨波逐浪句) (人天眼目 T48n2006; also J29nB244). (圜悟克勤) (recorded in 人天眼目 as 圓悟曰) glosses the first phrase with a (則)X(也) formula: (本真本空)。(一色一味)。(非無妙體)。(不在躊躇)。(洞然明白)。(則函蓋乾坤也) (T48n2006). In the record it is widely put as a test-question (如何是函蓋乾坤句) (54 occurrences in 33 allowlist texts) and answered variously (日出東方夜落西 T51n2077/X78n1556; 遍界黑漫漫 J25nB175; 吞吐虛空 J25nB171), and carried by verse-commentary (函蓋乾坤體自然，箇中原不著毫端; 函蓋乾坤事莫窮，頭頭物物露真風). The texts assign the phrase no gloss beyond the literal image and the (則)X(也) lines quoted above, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: The three-phrase set (雲門三句) = (函蓋乾坤) · (截斷眾流) · (隨波逐浪). Structural facts (describe-only): (1) the phrase originates in Yunmen's own (示眾) as one line of the triad (函蓋乾坤)、(目機銖兩)、(不涉萬緣) (春緣 in T47n1988); the numbered (三句) framing and the phrase-name (函蓋乾坤句) are the systematization of his heir (德山緣密), recorded in (人天眼目) and the lamp/(語錄) texts. (2) ORTHOGRAPHIC VARIANT: the water-radical form (涵蓋乾坤) occurs once in the allowlist (J40nB472), there in a different phrase (有時芥子藏身，有時涵蓋乾坤), not the (雲門三句) context. Do not cross-attribute the retold cases: Yunmen's own (示眾) (T47n1988) vs. the compiler-systematized exposition (人天眼目) vs. later (上堂) that merely raise the three (五燈會元 昔日雲門有三句).

Occurrences.Kwic: 函蓋乾坤目機銖兩。不涉春緣。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (雲門匡真禪師廣錄) (Yunmen's own Extended Record); a (示眾云) (示眾云…作麼生承當。代云。一鏃破三關). Yunmen's own record, single-speaker instruction — the primary source of the phrase. This Taisho edition reads (不涉春緣); other witnesses (T48n2006, J29nB244) read (不涉萬緣). KWIC is verbatim; it begins after (示眾云天中) — (天中) is the Taisho main-text reading (apparatus note 0563002: 天中＝大眾【明】), excluded from the KWIC.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師示眾云。函蓋乾坤。目機銖兩。不涉萬緣。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Eye of Humans and Gods (人天眼目), Yunmen-house section compiled by Huiyan Zhizhao. The preceding biographical paragraph identifies 'the master' as Yunmen Wenyan; Yunmen is the exact speaker who addresses the assembly with 'enclosing heaven and earth, judging the pivotal opportunity to the smallest weight, not involving the myriad conditions.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 函蓋乾坤事莫窮，頭頭物物露真風
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanshan Lai (三山來禪師語錄): in his Five Houses verses, Sanshan Denglai begins his verse on the first of Yunmen's three phrases by saying that the business of box-lid covering heaven and earth is inexhaustible.

Occurrences.Kwic: 昔日雲門有三句。謂函蓋乾坤句。截斷眾流
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): in Jiuding Jixing Huiquan's explicitly headed section, Jiuding Jixing Huiquan introduces Yunmen's three phrases and names the phrase that covers heaven and earth before the phrase that cuts off all streams.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問。如何是函蓋乾坤句。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元), Xichan Qin section. An unnamed monk questioning Xichan Qin is the exact speaker who asks for the line that covers heaven and earth; Xichan answers, ‘the stars in heaven all turn toward the north.’ All six attribution rungs leave the monk personally unnamed.
